# Kaṭāhakajātaka (Ja 125)

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
The *Kaṭāhakajātaka* (Ja 125) is a narrative in the Pali Jātaka collection [SuttaCentral; Fausböll 1877]. Set at Jetavana, the frame story relates that the Buddha told the tale concerning a boastful monk (*vikatthika bhikkhu*) who was prone to empty bragging and finding fault with others [SuttaCentral; Fausböll 1877; Burlingame 1921b]. The Dhammapada Commentary also cites the Jātaka in connection with a novice of humble origins who boasted about his kinsfolk [Burlingame 1921a; Burlingame 1921b].
In the story of the past, the Bodhisatta is a wealthy merchant (*seṭṭhi*) in Vārāṇasī during the reign of King Brahmadatta [Fausböll 1877]. His slave, named Kaṭāhaka, learns elite mercantile skills—including writing, warehouse keeping, business transactions, polite etiquette, and refined connoisseurship regarding food, dress, and perfume [Loukota; Fausböll 1877]. Using forged letters, Kaṭāhaka runs away and successfully passes himself off as the merchant's son to a family in a frontier region (*paccantavāsikā*), marrying into a prominent local household [Loukota; Fausböll 1877]. However, his snobbery and complaints about food lead to his undoing: the Bodhisatta discovers his whereabouts and conveys a cautionary verse—"One may boast ever so much, living in a foreign land, / But another will follow and spoil it all; eat your food, therefore, Kaṭāhaka" (*Bahuṃ pi so vikattheyyā...*) [Burlingame 1921b; Fausböll 1877]. Recognising the veiled warning, Kaṭāhaka subdues his pride, curbs his fastidious complaints, and eats whatever he is given [Fausböll 1877]. The Buddha concludes by identifying the boastful monk with Kaṭāhaka and himself with the merchant [Fausböll 1877].
Neither SuttaCentral nor DharmaNexus lists any direct early parallels or significant text-reuse matches for this Jātaka in other Buddhist corpora [SuttaCentral; DharmaNexus].
